source.snippet: If PoW (proof-of-work) schemes like Anubis ultimately don't work in practice, because Bots/Crawlers are increasingly using headless browsers, are able to solve captures, proofs, etc; What options do we have realistically to filter out or block unwanted traffic? What clever schemes can we come up that don't rely on centralised services like Cloudflare?

problem_statement: Website and SaaS operators need effective bot/crawler traffic filtering that does not depend on Cloudflare or other centralized third-party services, but existing PoW and CAPTCHA approaches are increasingly defeated by headless-browser bots.
target_segment: Indie SaaS operators, self-hosted web service owners, and small engineering teams running public-facing web properties who pay for bandwidth and compute consumed by bot traffic.
notes: Poster explicitly rejects Cloudflare dependency, signalling willingness to pay for an independent solution. Business context: operators absorb real compute/bandwidth costs from unwanted traffic. Pattern recurs across HN threads on Anubis and bot-blocking. Buyer signal: infrastructure owners who already pay Cloudflare or suffer without it.
